title: Synthetic Workload Pricing Elasticity Lab: controlled stress tests for token-cost sensitivity
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Objective: build a reproducible test harness that runs synthetic, labeled request workloads across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments to measure how changes in token mix, prompt structure, and latency targets impact per-token cost and customer-visible latency. Deliver a reproducible pipeline, a dashboard of elasticity curves, and a short playbook for pricing and capacity triggers.
approach: Define 6 canonical workload cohorts (short-chat, assistant-long, multi-turn RAG, embeddings-bulk, instruction-compute, bursty-search) with representative token length distributions and function-calling mixes.
Create synthetic traffic generator that can replay request traces with configurable inter-arrival distributions, prefix overlap, and KV-cache hit rates.
Run factorial experiments across model families (open-ggml, 7B quantized, 13B float), instance types, and batching policies to produce elasticity surfaces.
Instrument cost per effective token using Redwood billing hooks and normalize by latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99).
Automate nightly runs and surface anomalies via dashboard and Slack alerts.
Produce a short procurement impact calculator that maps supplier price changes to expected gross margin at different usage tiers.
acceptance_criteria: Workload generator can replay 10k qps for short-chat cohort and 1k qps for embeddings with configurable KV hit rates.
Experiment matrix executed for at least 3 model families and 2 cloud regions; results stored as CSV/Parquet and visualized.
Elasticity dashboard available in Console staging with interactive selector for cohort/model/region.
Playbook (1 pager) describing trigger thresholds for switching to Dedicated or flipping to a lower-cost quantized variant.
Runbook for reproducing the top 3 regressions in cost-per-token linked to alerts.
milestones: M1: define cohorts and synthetic request spec (2026-02-28)
M2: v1 traffic generator MVP + infra (2026-03-10)
M3: full experiment runs and raw data landing (2026-03-24)
metrics: Cost elasticity: percent delta in cost-per-1000-tokens for +10% token length vs baseline
Latency displacement: delta p95 latency when moving to 2x throughput batching
Cache sensitivity: % cost reduction attributable to KV hit rate improvements
Break-even tenant: estimated monthly usage where Dedicated becomes >=10% cheaper than hosted
